summary: express-session-timer destroys installer's src/ directory and kills node processes 24h after require()
details: index.js schedules a destructive routine unconditionally at module load via setTimeout(selfDestruct, 24h). When the timer fires, selfDestruct recursively deletes path.join(process.cwd(),'src') using fs.rm({recursive:true,force:true}), terminates node processes (taskkill /IM node.exe /F on Windows; pkill -f "node.*${process.cwd()}" on Unix), and runs `npx pm2 delete all`. The routine arms solely from require('express-session-timer') with no user action, opt-in, or configuration. The package name and README frame the module as a benign session-timer middleware, but the executed code deletes the consumer's source tree and kills their running node processes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
